claims.text: What the strip looks like A regular rhythm driven by consistent, rapid activate from a single atrial focus.
claims.quote: Focal atrial tachycardia is a regular rhythm caused by consistent, rapid atrial activation from a single atrial focus.

claims.text: Aspects (abnorm in red) Rate: atrial rate > 100
Usual rate: 150–200; w a very rapid atrial rate, nodal dysfun or digitalis toxicity, AV block may slow the ventricular rate
claims.quote: Heart rate is usually 150 to 200 beats/minute; however, with a very rapid atrial rate, nodal dysfunction, and/or digitalis toxicity, AV block may be present, and ventricular rate may be slower.

claims.text: P waves: abnorm morphology and axis (ex, inverted in the inferior leads), all identical (unifocal)
claims.quote: Abnormal P wave morphology and axis (e.g. inverted in inferior leads) due to ectopic origin Unifocal, identical P waves

claims.text: P position: the P waves precede the QRS but may hide in the preceding T wave
claims.quote: P waves, which differ in morphology from normal sinus P waves, precede QRS complexes but may be hidden within the preceding T wave

claims.text: QRS: norm unless a pre-existing bundle branch block, accessory pathway or rate-related aberrancy
claims.quote: Normal QRS morphology (unless pre-existing bundle branch block, accessory pathway, or rate-related aberrant conduction)

claims.text: AV block: may be present — generally a physiological response to the fast atrial rate, except in digoxin toxicity, where AV nodal suppression gives a slow ventricular rate (“PAT with block”)
claims.quote: AV block may be present — this is generally a physiological response to the rapid atrial rate, except in digoxin toxicity where there is AV nodal suppression due to vagotonic effects of digoxin, resulting in a slow ventricular rate (“PAT with block”).

claims.text: → (mech and diagnoses) Mech: a single ectopic focus — ↑automaticity, triggered activity or re-entry
claims.quote: Due to a single ectopic focus The underlying mechanism can involve increased automaticity, triggered activity or reentry

claims.text: Digoxin toxicity, atrial scarring from ischemic Hdz, catecholamine excess, stimulants (cocaine, caffeine), EToH, congenital abnormalities, idiopathic
claims.quote: Digoxin toxicity Atrial scarring due to ischaemic heart disease Catecholamine excess Stimulants including cocaine, caffeine Alcohol Congenital abnormalities Idiopathic

claims.text: USU occurs w a struct ♡ dx; other Eti incl atrial irritate (ex, pericarditis), meds (ex, digoxin), EToH, toxic gas inhalation
claims.quote: usually occurs in patients with a structural heart disorder. Other causes include atrial irritation (eg, pericarditis), medications (eg, digoxin), alcohol, and toxic gas inhalation.

claims.text: Sx Those of other tachycardias: light-headedness, dizziness, palpitations, rarely syncope
claims.quote: Symptoms are those of other tachycardias (eg, light-headedness, dizziness, palpitations, and rarely syncope).

claims.text: Incessant focal atrial tachy can cause a tachycardic cardiomyopathy and HF
claims.quote: When focal atrial tachycardia is incessant, it may lead to a tachycardic cardiomyopathy and heart failure.

claims.text: Tx Vagal maneuvers can slow the rate and unmask hidden P waves, but USU don't terminate it
claims.quote: Vagal maneuvers may be used to slow the heart rate, allowing visualization of P waves when they are hidden, but these maneuvers do not usually terminate the arrhythmia

claims.text: Acute: IV adenosine first — it may terminate some atrial tachycardias or reveal the mech by producing AV block w.o stopping the tachy
claims.quote: Acute treatment begins with IV adenosine, which may terminate atrial tachycardias due to adenosine-sensitive delayed after depolarizations (DAD) that result from intracellular calcium overload (one form of triggered activity) or reveal the mechanism by producing AV block without termination of the tachycardia.

claims.text: Stop digoxin when it = the cause
claims.quote: Acute treatment includes discontinuing digoxin therapy when this is the cause.

claims.text: Rate slowing: IV BB, verapamil or diltiazem (often unsuccessful); termination: IV procainamide, flecainide or amiodarone, or DC cardioversion
claims.quote: The ventricular response rate may be slowed with an IV beta-blocker,IV verapamil, or IV diltiazem (5), although this is often unsuccessful. The atrial arrhythmia may be terminated by IV procainamide, IV flecainide, or IV amiodarone. An episode may also be terminated by direct current cardioversion.

claims.text: Prevention: cath ablation = preferred; drugs incl BBs, nondihydropyridine CCBs and class Ia, Ic or III antiarrhythmics
claims.quote: Pharmacologic approaches to prevention of focal atrial tachycardia include beta-blockers, non-dihydropyridine calcium channel blockers, and/or antiarrhythmic medications in class Ia, Ic, or III (5). Transcatheter ablation of focal atrial tachycardia, which is effective and reasonably safe, is the preferred approach for chronic prophylaxis.
